items.title: Pay customs/handling fee to release parcel
items.computation: The letter states a specific calendar due date (09.11.2026), not a period to be counted. Since this is presented as a payment demand from a private-sounding entity (payee 'Intl. Parcel Clearing Ltd.' differs from the letterhead sender), the date is used exactly as printed, with no weekend/holiday adjustment rule applicable to a stated calendar date. 09.11.2026 is a Monday, so no adjustment would be needed regardless.

warnings: This letter shows strong hallmarks of a parcel/customs scam: the payee named in the payment box, 'Intl. Parcel Clearing Ltd.', does not match the sender printed in the letterhead, 'Paketzentrum Musterstadt – Zollabwicklung' — genuine German customs (Zoll) never routes payment through a differently-named private company.

Genuine German customs authorities do not instruct recipients to raise queries exclusively via WhatsApp ('Rückfragen bitte ausschließlich per WhatsApp an 0176 5530 2291'); this is a common pressure/anonymity tactic used in parcel-delivery scams.

The sender's email domain, 'clearance-mail.example', uses the reserved/placeholder top-level domain '.example', which is never used for real correspondence — a strong sign this is a template or fabricated document.

The itemized charges are internally inconsistent: the 'Einfuhrumsatzsteuer' (import VAT) line shows no amount, 'Bearbeitungsentgelt Zollabwicklung' is listed as 21,40, and 'Zu zahlen' shows 17,50, yet the total charged is 38,90 — the breakdown does not add up transparently, typical of a hastily constructed fake invoice.

The short deadline (only a few days) combined with a threat to return or destroy the parcel is a classic urgency/pressure tactic used in scam letters; do not pay or transfer money to the IBAN given without independently verifying any actual shipment and contacting the real sender/carrier through official channels first.

There is no verifiable official reference such as a real customs 'Bescheidnummer' or postal carrier tracking confirmation, and the recipient's address (Neu-Beispielstadt) and sender's address (Musterstadt) appear unrelated, further suggesting this is not a genuine authority or carrier communication.
